data.title: BPCL Q2 profit drops 21 pc to Rs 4,863 crore; revenue rises nearly 30 pc
data.description:
New Delhi, Oct. 24 -- State-run Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) reported a 21 per cent year-on-year decline in consolidated net profit to Rs 4,863.05 crore in the second quarter of financial year 2026-27 (Q2 FY27), while its revenue from operations surged nearly 30 per cent, according to a statement issued by the Maharatna company.

As per the release, BPCL's consolidated revenue from operations rose 29.78 per cent year-on-year to Rs 1,57,818 crore in Q2 FY27 from Rs 1,21,605 crore in the corresponding quarter of FY26. However, consolidated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) declined 13.37 per cent to Rs 9,647 crore from Rs 11,136 crore, while net profit fell 21.45 per cent to Rs 4,863 crore from Rs 6,191 crore.

On a standalone basis, the company's revenue from operations increased 29.78 per cent to Rs 1,57,779 crore from Rs 1,21,571 crore in the year-ago period. Meanwhile, standalone EBITDA declined 13.96 per cent to Rs 9,437 crore, while net profit dropped 22.50 per cent to Rs 4,993 crore from Rs 6,443 crore in Q2 FY26.

On the operational front, BPCL reported refinery throughput of 10.41 million metric tonnes (MMT) in Q2 FY27, with capacity utilisation reaching 118 per cent.

Apart from this, "During the quarter, BPCL expanded its LPG and PNG network, enhanced customer amenities and advanced indigenous technology and alternative fuel solutions," the company said in a release.

The company's domestic market sales stood at 13.47 MMT during the quarter. BPCL also continued investments in infrastructure development, strengthening supply chain resilience and digital transformation.

Meanwhile, BPCL strengthened its strategic partnerships and advanced plans for the proposed Ramayapatnam Refinery and Petrochemical Complex, with its board approving the incorporation of a dedicated project company.

The Maharatna PSU also continued to focus on improving operational efficiency, product quality and customer safety while pursuing initiatives aimed at meeting India's evolving energy requirements. It "Connected 1.22 lakh new homes to Piped Natural Gas (PNG) in the last six months."

BPCL shares closed at Rs 281.25 per share, down 5.25 points or 1.83 per cent on Friday.

WUHU, China, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- During Chery International User Summit 2026, CHERY held a family parking challenge carnival at Squirrel Town. Centred on SIVP (Super Intelligent Valet Parking), it combined a parking workshop, scenario challenges and hands-on experiences, showing global guests how intelligent parking can save families time and effort.

A Parking Technology Class Introduces SIVP as the Latest Expression of “Technology. For Family”

At the parking workshop, CHERY presented three “For Family” pillars: “Space. For Family”, “Safety. For Family” and “Technology. For Family”. Guests had experienced the first two through vehicle experiences and a crash-test challenge; SIVP brought the third to life.

CHERY Brand Director Leo Liu counted the 27 sensors on the TIGGO7 together with users on site.

CHERY’s global user research found that parking and finding a space can affect a family’s mood. In supported, mapped car parks, SIVP offers two functions: One Tap Departure lets users select a pick-up point in the app and request the vehicle to travel there; One Step Home assists with parking after users get out. Users must follow app instructions, monitor the vehicle and surroundings, and remain ready to pause or take over.

SIVP uses AI Planner and an end-to-end large model to plan movements, avoid obstacles and respond to changing situations. It marks the first large-scale overseas application of such a model in production vehicles. Its 3R11V12U1L configuration—three millimetre-wave radars, 11 high-definition cameras, 12 ultrasonic sensors and one lidar—provides 360-degree sensing, helping detect obstacles in complex parking spaces and giving families greater peace of mind.

Timed Family Challenges Compare Parking and Vehicle Pick-up

Twelve guests drew lots to form four temporary families, each playing a father, mother and child. Timed challenges compared the SIVP and control groups.

The “Monday Morning Rush” recreated the pressure of getting children ready and leaving early. Each family had to complete a sequence of tasks, including preparing breakfast, tying a tie and helping their child through breakfast, before getting into the car together. The SIVP group could summon the vehicle to the door in advance using a phone, then get straight in once the tasks were finished, avoiding a detour to collect it. The “Easier Family Shopping Challenge” recreated a supermarket trip. The SIVP group could get out and head into the shop, using the app to initiate valet parking, then summon the vehicle back after shopping. The control group had to park manually and carry their purchases back to the car park to find their vehicle. The comparison showed clearly how much time and effort could be saved when parking and collecting a car.

Hands-On Experiences Across Multiple Models Bring Family Feedback into Focus

In the open experience area, guests could visit different zones offering Automatic Parking Assist (APA) demonstrations and SIVP experiences in challenging spaces, including bays at the end of dead-end parking aisles and extremely narrow bays. These activities showcased SIVP’s ability to handle complex parking scenarios. Afterwards, guests completed questionnaires about their experiences. Their feedback will inform ongoing improvements to SIVP, bringing intelligent parking technology closer to families’ actual mobility needs.

From technical explanations in the classroom and clear comparisons in the challenges to hands-on operation in the experience area, the carnival demonstrated CHERY’s understanding of families through the everyday act of parking. Parking need no longer be a burden on family outings, and every minute saved can be spent with loved ones. Through SIVP, “Technology. For Family” is becoming part of daily life for more families.

data.title: Typhoon Champi sweeps past Taiwan, leaving 1 dead, 500 injured
data.description:
Key points:
  • One person swept away by waves in Taiwan
  • Champi heading north, not expected to directly strike China
  • Autumn typhoons are relatively rare

By Yimou Lee and Ann Wang

Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday, killing 1 person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continued to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast though it was not expected to make landfall there.

At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi is weakening though still packing gusts of around 126 kph (78 mph) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration.

The storm was about 150 km (93 miles) east of Taiwan, having glanced off the island's northeastern coast in Yilan County early on Saturday, the CWA said.

The centre of the storm turned south around midnight, hugging the Yilan coastline before making a rare loop offshore and moving northward away, triggering gusts of about 227 kph (141 mph) in some coastal areas, knocking down power lines and sending roof tiles flying.

'MOST TERRIFYING AROUND MIDNIGHT'

"It was most terrifying around midnight," said a retired teacher surnamed Lin as he inspected downed banana trees in his garden in Yilan. "It was a sleepless night. I haven't seen anything like this in many years."

The storm's forecast track shows it turning north, tracking up the Chinese coast and eventually moving into southern Japan.

Taiwan's fire department said the death toll remained at 1, a man swept away by waves from the island of Liuqiu, with 527 injuries during the heavy wind and torrential rain.

Taipower said at one point more than 288,000 homes had lost electricity, though most had been reconnected.

The transport ministry said 242 flights were cancelled, an improvement from Friday, when the number was almost 1,000.

In the capital Taipei, there were downed trees and on-off squally rain showers.

A swathe of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second day of office and school closures on Saturday.

Taiwan is generally well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too.

China's emergency management ministry sent a team to the eastern province of Zhejiang as Champi approached, warning of strong winds and heavy rain through Sunday. It said 400 rescue workers and 600 pieces of equipment had been readied, while more than 41,000 firefighters were on emergency duty.

In Taizhou, a city on Zhejiang's coast, more than 3,800 fishing boats returned to harbour, offshore fish-farm workers were brought ashore and 2,084 island visitors were evacuated, state media reported.

Authorities halted 25 offshore construction projects and suspended 18 passenger ferry routes.

data.title: AbbVie Gains FDA Approval For Subcutaneous Induction Of SKYRIZI In Crohn's Disease
data.description:
WASHINGTON (dpa-AFX) - AbbVie (ABBV) announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved a subcutaneous induction regimen for SKYRIZI (risankizumab-rzaa) for adults with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease, providing patients with a new option to begin treatment at home.

The approval is supported by positive results from the Phase 3 AFFIRM trial, which evaluated the efficacy and safety of subcutaneous SKYRIZI versus placebo in patients with moderately to severely active Crohn's disease. The study met its co-primary endpoints, with SKYRIZI demonstrating superiority in achieving both clinical remission and endoscopic response at Week 12.

With the newly approved subcutaneous induction regimen, patients can start SKYRIZI treatment at home using an on-body injector (OBI) induction pack and continue maintenance treatment with an OBI every eight weeks. The SC induction dosing schedule consists of 720 mg administered at Weeks 0, 2, 4 and 8. Patients may also choose the previously approved intravenous induction regimen of 600 mg at Weeks 0, 4 and 8 before transitioning to maintenance dosing beginning at Week 12.

AbbVie said the approval expands flexibility for patients and healthcare providers by offering a fully subcutaneous treatment pathway from induction through maintenance.

In addition, the FDA approved an update to SKYRIZI's prescribing information across all approved indications. The revised warning and precautions language advises healthcare providers to consider tuberculosis (TB) evaluation before treatment initiation based on clinical judgment. The update removes any requirement for mandatory TB testing prior to starting SKYRIZI, giving physicians greater flexibility in patient assessment while maintaining appropriate safety oversight.

ABBV closed Friday's regular trading at $285.64 up $0.45 or 0.16%.

data.title: 2026 iCAUR International User Summit Opens in Wuhu, Bringing Together Future Classic Design, Customization and User Co-Creation
data.description:
Key points:
  • The 2026 iCAUR International User Summit opened on October 19 in Wuhu, China, under the theme “Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours.”
  • The iCAUR V25 made its global debut and officially went on sale worldwide. Together with the V23 and V27, it rounds out the V-Series lineup, bringing the Future Classic Design concept to life across a comprehensive product portfolio.
  • Three officially customized V-Series models will enter global markets. At the summit, 20 customized vehicles were showcased, highlighting the creativity of users from different communities and markets.

WUHU, China, Oct. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- The 2026 iCAUR International User Summit opened in Wuhu, China, on October 19, bringing together more than 500 user representatives from around the world, alongside partners and international media. Under the theme “Classic Never Fades | Make It Yours,” the five-day event brings together product experiences, vehicle customization, user stories and ecosystem activities, highlighting how iCAUR connects its design philosophy with the interests and creativity of users around the world.

The summit showcases the iCAUR V25, three officially customized V-Series models, and 20 customized vehicles. Visitors can also explore the iCAUR brand showroom, take part in a smart factory tour, and experience the V-Series through multi-scenario test drives. The event also marks the introduction of iCAUR’s first group of Brand Ambassadors and highlights the next phase of its global user engagement initiative, Club Connect. Through these activities, iCAUR brings together three key elements of its brand: Future Classic Design, customization and a growing network of users who help shape the brand’s development.

 [A Bustling Scene from 2026 iCAUR International User Summit]

Building a Global Brand Through Products and Local Connections

Since its launch, iCAUR has expanded into more than 40 countries and regions worldwide. The V23 has surpassed 100,000 units in cumulative global sales and received the Red Dot Design Award in 2026, while the V27 won the Best Interior Design Award in the Premium Car Category at the 2026 Torino Automotive Design Award (TADA).

These milestones mark an important stage in the brand’s international development. As iCAUR continues to expand into new markets, it is also working with local partners to strengthen sales and service networks and build lasting relationships with users.

At the summit, Ronna, CEO of iCAUR International, shared the brand’s view that entering a market is only the beginning. Long-term growth comes from understanding users, listening to their ideas and creating experiences that give them more ways to engage with the brand.

iCAUR V25 Expands the V-Series

The iCAUR V25 takes center stage at the summit, further expanding the V-Series alongside the V23 and V27. Built around the brand’s Future Classic Design philosophy, the V25 combines a distinctive boxy silhouette and classic round headlights with modern technology and capabilities for a range of driving scenarios.

 [iCAUR V25 Global Debut]

At the event, Dr. Su Jun, Vice President of Chery Automobile Co., Ltd., explained the thinking behind the V25 through three principles: restraint, capability and freedom.

The design retains the V-Series’ recognizable proportions and signature styling rather than following short-term trends. Its i-SWIFT Agile Handling Platform, Golden REEV powertrain and i-AWD system support a variety of driving conditions, from urban roads to more challenging terrain.

The V25 also leaves room for personalization, with more than 20 ecosystem interfaces. Other features include a 1.8-ton towing capacity, 6 kW vehicle-to-load (V2L) capability, 66.4% space efficiency, 41 storage spaces and a body made of 80% high-strength steel.

Together, the V23, V25 and V27 show how Future Classic Design can take different forms across the V-Series, combining a recognizable design identity with modern technology and opportunities for personal expression.

Three Officially Customized Models Showcase Different Personalities

Customization is a key highlight of the summit, with three officially customized V-Series models presented alongside 20 customized vehicles developed with users and partners.

Each of the three officially customized models reflects a different interest and lifestyle. The V23 Forge brings urban individuality to life with a muscular widebody stance and gloss-black accents, while retaining the V23’s playful character. The V25 Game Changer celebrates the freedom to play, combining the V25’s classic toughness with gaming-inspired details. The V27 Sun Roam draws inspiration from 1980s off-road vehicles and vintage cameras, pairing rugged proportions with carefully crafted details.

 [Three Officially Customized iCAUR Models on Display]

The three models are planned for introduction in global markets by early 2027, through KD production or dealer-installed packages, subject to local regulations and market conditions. Beyond the official builds, the 20 customized vehicles on display demonstrate how users and partners bring their own ideas to the V-Series. Visitors can explore different styles, learn about customization details and exchange ideas with the teams behind the vehicles.

 [Global User Creativity at 2026 iCAUR International User Summit]

Customization is already an important part of the iCAUR user experience. According to the brand, 50% of its users worldwide customize their vehicles. Their choices and ideas also provide inspiration for the brand’s future products and customization offerings.

Looking ahead, iCAUR plans to introduce dedicated customization spaces in its showrooms, giving customers more opportunities to explore personalization options. The brand also plans to present a customized classic vehicle alongside new models at future model launches, offering inspiration for different ways to make an iCAUR their own.

The brand is continuing to expand its customized vehicle lineup, develop accessories suited to local markets and establish quality and safety validation mechanisms for customization offerings. These efforts aim to make customization more accessible while safeguarding quality and safety.

Connecting Vehicles with Lifestyle Experiences

The iCAUR brand showroom brings together vehicle customization, classic lifestyle elements, and user co-creation, offering visitors a broader view of the brand beyond its vehicles.

 [iCAUR Brand Ecosystem Showroom]

Body accessories, outdoor equipment and lifestyle products demonstrate how the vehicle can connect with different interests and everyday activities. Music, travel, surfing and cycling elements reflect the varied ways users explore their interests and express their individuality.

The summit also includes a smart factory tour, giving participants a closer look at iCAUR’s manufacturing processes and quality management. During the event, the V-Series multi-scenario test-drive activities will give participants the opportunity to experience the V25 and V27 across different road conditions, including wavy roads, mud, uneven terrain, S-curves and other driving challenges. Activities involving smart ecosystem partner AiMOGA and green community initiatives are also scheduled as part of the five-day program.

Together, these experiences allow users and partners to explore the vehicles, understand the brand’s design approach and see how iCAUR connects its products with different lifestyles and interests.

From Official User Clubs to Global Club Connect

For iCAUR, the relationship with users continues well beyond vehicle delivery. The brand has established official user clubs in nine countries, bringing owners together to share experiences and connect through common interests.

[2026 iCAUR International User Summit Bird View]

In 2027, iCAUR plans to expand this approach through its global Club Connect initiative, bringing together more users across markets, encouraging the exchange of ideas, and using user feedback to inform future products and experiences.

 [CAUR’s First Group of Brand Ambassadors]

The summit also marks the introduction of iCAUR’s first group of Brand Ambassadors. These users are recognized for their creativity, passion, and contributions to the brand. Through Club Connect, iCAUR plans to continue selecting ambassadors who can share their experiences, contribute to brand activities, and inspire other users in their markets.

User participation also extends to customization. Ideas from users may inspire future officially customized models for global markets, creating further opportunities for users to contribute to how iCAUR products evolve.

As the brand continues its international expansion, iCAUR aims to reach more than 70 markets by 2027. Alongside market development, it will continue working with local partners to strengthen sales and service networks and to develop user engagement in different regions.

The 2026 iCAUR International User Summit brings these priorities together through iCAUR’s vehicles, customized builds, hands-on experiences, and growing network of user clubs and Brand Ambassadors.

Guided by “Classic Never Fades” and “Make It Yours,” iCAUR continues to develop its Future Classic Design philosophy while giving users more opportunities to express their individuality and contribute to the brand. For iCAUR, delivery is not the end of the story, but the starting point for what users can make of their iCAUR.

About iCAUR

Chery Group's iCAUR is a new energy automotive brand driven by Future Classic Design and technology. Guided by its design philosophy, iCAUR combines classic design elements with modern aesthetics and technology to develop distinctive vehicles for urban mobility and outdoor exploration. With a focus on product innovation and customization, iCAUR offers diverse vehicle choices and personalization options, extending its brand experience through user services and a growing range of user engagements initiatives.

iCAUR’s product portfolio is supported by technologies including i-AWD intelligent electric all-wheel drive and the REEV Golden Range Extender, delivering performance and capability for a range of driving conditions. With a growing presence in more than 40 markets worldwide, iCAUR continues to expand its international business and user engagements, guided by its brand belief: Classic Never Fades.

data.title: Slate Grocery REIT Announces Receipt of Interim Order, and Provides Meeting and Circular Details
data.description:
Slate Grocery REIT (TSX: SGR.U) (TSX: SGR.UN) (the “REIT”), an owner and operator of U.S. grocery-anchored real estate, announced today that it has obtained an interim order (the “Interim Order”) of the Ontario Superior Court of Justice (Commercial List) (the “Court”) in connection with the proposed acquisition by EP/BRX Holdings LLC (the “Purchaser”), a joint venture between an affiliate of Brixmor Property Group Inc. and affiliates of Everview Partners, L.P., of all of the REIT’s issued and outstanding units pursuant to the terms and conditions of an arrangement agreement (the “Arrangement Agreement”) among the REIT, the Purchaser and 1001700324 Ontario Inc. dated September 27, 2026 (the “Arrangement”). The Arrangement was previously announced by the REIT on September 28, 2026.

Interim Order, Meeting and Circular

The Interim Order, granted on October 22, 2026, authorizes the calling and holding of a special meeting of unitholders of the REIT (the “Meeting”) to consider and vote on a special resolution approving the Arrangement. The Meeting is scheduled to be held in a virtual-only format on Wednesday, November 25, 2026 at 11:00 a.m. (Eastern time). Unitholders of record as of the close of business on October 20, 2026 will be entitled to receive notice of and vote at the Meeting.

The REIT expects to file its management information circular (the “Circular”) and related meeting materials on SEDAR+ on November 2, 2026 and to mail those materials to unitholders on or about November 2, 2026. The Circular will provide details of the Arrangement, the matters to be considered at the Meeting and the procedures for participating in and voting at the Meeting. Once filed, the Circular and related meeting materials will be available under the REIT’s profile on SEDAR+ at www.sedarplus.ca and on the REIT’s website at slategroceryreit.com. Unitholders are urged to read the Circular and related meeting materials carefully when they become available.

Other Matters

In connection with the Arrangement, the REIT has applied to the Ontario Securities Commission (the “OSC”) for discretionary exemptive relief from the requirement to obtain minority approval on a class-by-class basis under Multilateral Instrument 61-101 – Protection of Minority Security Holders in Special Transactions (“MI 61-101”) with a view to ensuring that the vote is structured in a manner that is fair to all unitholders. Under the REIT’s declaration of trust, holders of class A units, class I units and class U units generally vote together as a single class unless the business to be transacted affects holders of one class in a manner materially different from its effect on holders of another class. The REIT’s board of trustees has determined that the Arrangement does not have such a differential effect.

If the requested relief is granted, disinterested holders of class A units, class I units and class U units will vote on the Arrangement under MI 61-101 together as a single class, with one vote per unit, rather than separately by class. Votes required to be excluded under MI 61-101 will be excluded from that minority approval vote. There can be no assurance that the requested relief will be granted by the OSC.

The REIT’s declaration of trust permits the trustees of the REIT to require the conversion of all outstanding class A units or class I units into class U units if the number of outstanding units of the applicable class is less than 10% of the number of units of that class issued on the closing of the REIT’s initial public offering, which is currently the case for both the class A units and class I units. If the requested relief is not secured prior to the date that is 10 business days before the Meeting, all class A units and class I units will be converted into class U units, effective before the Meeting, pursuant to such provisions. Holders of class A units or class I units on the record date whose units are so converted will be deemed to have held those class U units on the record date, the whole in accordance with the terms of the REIT’s declaration of trust.

Completion of the Arrangement remains subject to the requisite unitholder approvals, including approval by at least two-thirds of the votes cast by unitholders voting together as a single class and the applicable minority approval under MI 61-101, receipt of the final order of the Court approving the Arrangement, receipt of the required approval under the Investment Canada Act, and the satisfaction or waiver of the other conditions to closing set out in the Arrangement Agreement. Subject to obtaining the necessary approvals and satisfying or waiving the other closing conditions, the Arrangement is expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027.

data.description:
Exchange-traded funds that use options strategies are among the fastest-growing actively managed products. Many are geared to people hoping to smooth out their returns or get more income than they would from bonds. Others seek to take advantage of the volatility of a single stock or other asset.

By Debbie Carlson

Born out of the low-interest-rate era and during a time when stock market volatility left some investors nervous, so-called buffer and covered-call ETFs offer a way for skittish investors to stay in the market or get monthly income. These strategies now have close to $300 billion in assets, from near zero in 2020, according to data from Morningstar and Baird Strategas.

But there's no free lunch in markets. Buffer and covered-call ETFs sell call options, which give buyers the right to purchase an underlying asset at a set price and time. The ETFs give up some upside to buy downside protection or fund regular payouts, or distributions, so they lag behind broader markets when there are strong rallies. They're complex and price opaque, and some buyers may be taking more risk than they realize. Some narrowly focused ETFs, such as single-stock ETFs, are prone to wild swings in returns — sometimes over just a few days.

Buffer ETFs

Buffer ETFs are the least risky of these products. They use options to provide partial downside protection, thus the term "buffer," in exchange for a cap on gains over a fixed period. The most popular ones protect buyers from the first 10% of losses of a benchmark, such as the S&P 500 index. New ones are released monthly, with varying levels of downside protection, so there can be dozens available at the same time.

Financial pros call buffer funds a real innovation for the risk-averse. Scott Opsal, director of research at the Leuthold Group, says using the proceeds from selling call options to buy some downside protection is a legitimate trade-off. "You get more upside than a bond, and if the market wobbles, you can ignore it. That's a true behavior changer for risk-averse investors," he says.

Yet investors may also still lose money if markets fall below the buffer level, warns Nate Geraci, president of NovaDius Wealth Management. Also, investors who buy these at a midpoint during the fixed period might find that their cap and buffer levels are different from what's advertised.

Covered-Call ETFs

Covered-call ETFs are somewhat more risky. They sell call options to give investors an income stream today at the expense of letting share price grow and compound over time to create a bigger investment.

Their selling points are attractive distribution rates, such as the 8% offered by the $45 billion JPMorgan Equity Premium Income ETF, the largest of these funds by assets.

The strategies work best in choppy, range-bound markets where there's little price appreciation but meaningful volatility, says Todd Sohn, chief ETF strategist at Baird Strategas. Options are priced partially on implied volatility, which reflects the options market's expectation of how far and how fast an underlying security will move over a specific time frame. Larger-than-expected market swings tend to fatten premiums and increase income.

For retirees who have ridden the stock bull market of the past few decades, using broad-based covered-call strategies to tap income makes sense, Sohn says. In the past few years, broad-based options-income ETFs have delivered more yield and were less volatile than long-dated bond ETFs, which tumbled in value during the sharp rise in interest rates.

Investors should be aware that if the benchmark asset falls, these ETFs will also fall, albeit slightly less than the underlying asset because of the yield cushion. They also don't rebound in line with benchmark gains because the upside was sold away.

Over time, the net asset value and price return can lag behind the benchmark, a common criticism of these funds. For example, Equity Income's three-year annualized return is 10.7% versus the S&P 500's three-year annualized return of 22.8%.

Hamilton Reiner, head of U.S. equity derivatives at J.P. Morgan Equity Asset Management, says in years like 2026, when there's a strong bull market, the JPMorgan Equity Income ETF lags behind. It won't outperform the index over a market cycle, but he expects it to have better risk-adjusted returns, since it is designed to be less volatile.

Investors should look at the strategy on a total-return basis, including income, and not just at price or net asset value. For Equity Income, Reiner says that over the past three years, distributions have been about 8% a year, with the 2% to 3% remaining being price appreciation.

Single-Stock and Non-Equity Income Strategies

The success of broad-based option-income ETFs have spawned other categories, including ones based on single stocks, gold, and Bitcoin. These are riskier because they aren't diversified, and are often more volatile than a broad index. But since options become more valuable as volatility increases, these ETFs can offer high payouts.

"Be cautious or extremely cautious of those types of things," says Dan Sotiroff, associate director of manager research at Morningstar.

The largest single-stock income ETF by assets is the $1.3 billion YieldMax NVDA Option Income Strategy. This ETF uses call spreads — that is, it sells a call on Nvidia stock to collect the options premium for income, and buys a higher-priced call, which preserves more upside during sharp rallies than traditional covered-call ETFs. A year ago, it also changed its income payout to every week from monthly.

The fund holds a mix of U.S. Treasuries, plus monthly and weekly options on Nvidia stock, but not the stock itself. The weekly options can react more sharply to stock moves than longer-dated options, even though the stock isn't more volatile. The payout is more variable since the strategy resets every week. As of Oct. 15, the listed distribution was 33%.

Some YieldMax ETFs have much higher distribution rates, such as the $1.1 billion YieldMax MSTR Option Income Strategy, which buys and sells options on Strategy stock and had an 82.9% distribution rate as of Oct. 15.

Mike Khouw, a strategist at YieldMax, says when looking at ETFs with high distributions, investors should consider the distribution rate against a reference asset's realistic rate of return to judge whether they think it is too risky. "If you see a very high yield in bonds, that tells you that there's probably something a little bit riskier there," he says.

These are for high-conviction, active traders who prize cash flow over total return and expect a stock to trade range-bound for a short time frame.

Autocallable ETFs

There's a new category of complex options-income strategy ETFs that also offers high payouts. Generally, autocallable ETFs ladder a series of options tied to equity markets, either an index like the S&P 500 or a single stock, created to give stable payouts as long as the options stay above a customized downside barrier, but investors give up any price gains.

The barriers are often set very low, such as a 40% loss. However, if the barrier is broken, investors lose everything. Some ETFs, such as the $1.4 billion Calamos Autocallable Income, the first of these to launch a year ago, diversify by laddering more than 50 individual options to reduce that risk. As of Sept. 30, it had a monthly 14.3% distribution rate.

Option-focused ETFs became popular when bond yields were low a few years ago and picked up steam during 2022's bond rout, when bond funds lost money. Now, with the 10-year U.S. Treasury yielding 5.1% and investment-grade bonds yielding 5.8%, income investors have more options.

Geraci says with bonds yielding more and providing their traditional ballast to stocks, investors could simplify their portfolios by owning lower-cost stock ETFs and manage the equity risk with high-quality bonds or other assets, rather than buying these option-strategy ETFs and paying their higher fees.

"It's easy to point to 2022 as a reason to avoid bonds, but investors have to remember, that was a historically bad year for fixed income. I don't believe investors should approach portfolio construction by simply focusing on outlier years," he says.

Reiner says the higher bond yields create competition across asset classes for investors' dollars, but he still sees room for options strategies in portfolios.

"At their current levels, bonds are attractive," Reiner says. But he argues that options-based ETFs provide income without credit spread or duration risk — both of which can bite bondholders — and can serve as a complement to stocks and bonds, even though they limit potential upside.

With all these ETFs, distribution rates are sometimes referred to as yields, but the financial experts warn that these payouts aren't like traditional bond payouts where coupons are fixed. Distribution rates aren't guaranteed returns and shouldn't be equated with a bond yield.

Reiner also stresses that these aren't bond replacements and don't play that role. "Bonds are bonds. Stocks are stocks. This is somewhere in between," he says. "These may help you create a different source of return from a well-balanced portfolio."

data.title: Iran's Hostage Playbook And What to Do Now — Barron's
data.description:
By Steven M. Sears

Elevated oil prices, a primary driver of inflation, could last until President Donald Trump leaves the White House, according to Michael Schwartz, the dean of Wall Street's options strategists. Schwartz believes the Iranian regime is using the 1979-1981 hostage playbook to guide decisions during the current crisis with the U.S. Back then, Iran waited until Ronald Reagan defeated Jimmy Carter and was inaugurated to release hostages taken by students who stormed the U.S. embassy in Tehran.

"The Iranian terror regime will do everything it can to harm America, and interfering with the free flow of oil through the Strait of Hormuz is an effective way to increase global inflationary pressures, influence central bank policy, and even interfere with domestic U.S. politics," Schwartz, Oppenheimer's chief options strategist, told Barron's.

His views are informed by his nearly unrivaled experience helping clients navigate the markets. He was trading options before options were first listed on an exchange in 1973. As Wall Street's longest-tenured options strategist, he has been instrumental in the growth and development of the market.

While many investors hope Iran seeks a peaceful solution to the current standoff, Schwartz says that the longer Iran resists the U.S., the more respected Iran becomes in the Middle East. Also, Iran's influence over the Strait of Hormuz has exposed an American weakness: The economy needs oil, and Iran has an outsize influence on oil prices and supply that is difficult for America to control.

The Iran hostage crisis was so long ago that many active investors weren't yet born, or were too young to remember it. But Iranian revolutionaries captivated the world when they toppled the shah, who was backed by the U.S. The revolutionaries stormed the U.S. embassy and took hostages. The hard-liners, who are the ideological parents of the present regime, were angry that President Carter let the Shah visit America for cancer treatment. America froze Iran's financial assets, but Iran diplomatically embarrassed America. For 444 days, despite a failed special-forces rescue, Americans were held hostage. Since then, Iran, a founding member of OPECs, has grown stronger and emerged as a global terrorism sponsor, Schwartz says.

During the hostage crisis, oil prices doubled to more than $39 a barrel in 1980 from about $15 in 1979. America's inflation surged. Since the Iran conflict began in February, Brent crude has increased to about $107 a barrel from about $65.

Paul Volcker, appointed Federal Reserve chairman just before the embassy attack, was forced to sharply increase interest rates to battle inflation. By 1980, U.S. interest rates were about 18%, a level so high, Schwartz says, that many investors turned away from stocks to buy bonds. The Fed recently raised rates to control inflation, and some market watchers have expressed concern that Volcker's playbook could be resurrected.

To trade Iran's playbook, Schwartz says investors can consider a December 2028 call-spread trade. The strategy, which entails buying one call option and selling another with a higher strike but the same expiration, allows investors to use a small amount of money — relative to buying shares outright — to position for a relief rally that Schwartz expects will occur when Trump leaves office.

With the State Street S&P 500 SPDR exchange-traded fund at $768.73, Schwartz suggests buying the December $825 call and selling the December $875 call, both of which expire in 2028. At $875, the maximum profit of the spread is $25. If the ETF is below $825 at expiration, the trade fails.

During the past 52 weeks, the ETF has ranged from $629.28 to $781.62.

To lower the cost of the trade, Schwartz says that investors can sell the December $615 put option for about $23.

"History may not repeat, but it often rhymes, and that often creates opportunity for investors," Schwartz says. "This strategy is intended to monetize that phenomenon."

data.title: Income Investing: Taxes Are on the Ballot. That Could Be Bad News for Munis. — Barron's
data.description:
By Randall W. Forsyth

Affordability is the buzzword heard throughout this election season, but it isn't confined to the midterm congressional contests. At the state level, an array of pocketbook propositions are on the ballot — and they don't concern just the constituents voting on the questions. Their outcome could also affect far-flung investors in municipal bonds issued in those states and localities.

Many propositions are aimed at capping taxes, which has obvious appeal to those paying them but could undercut the revenue that pays the interest and principal on bonds that fund public services and infrastructure. Other voters are being asked to approve or extend levies on the wealthiest taxpayers, which could bolster funding for public purposes but also induce the rich to exit for more tax-friendly climes.

Of the latter, California's so-called billionaire tax has gotten the most notice. The Golden State's Proposition 40 would impose a one-time 5% tax on assets over $1 billion to help fund healthcare, education, and food-assistance programs.

On the opposite coast, Florida voters will consider the "Save Our Homes From Excessive Property Taxes" amendment. That would increase the "homestead exemption" to $250,000 by 2028, from $50,000 currently.

These two high-profile propositions exemplify the principle made famous decades ago by Sen. Russell Long, a powerful Louisiana Democrat who headed the Senate Finance Committee from 1966 to 1981: "Don't tax you, don't tax me, tax the fellow behind the tree!"

The California billionaire tax would obviously hit just the few in this rarefied cohort, with the equally obvious intent to redistribute part of their wealth.

The Sunshine State's property-tax exemption would be reserved for Florida residents who have owned their homes for at least five years. So, new residents, or those with Florida vacation homes (and thus don't vote there), are left out of the largess.

As for bond investors, the impact of such schemes is uncertain, even if they gain voter approval.

There may be an estimated 200 billionaires in California, Dan Close, head of municipals at Nuveen, told Barron's, but added that he doubted they all would leave. One who may opt to stay put is Meta Platforms CEO Mark Zuckerberg. Terms of Meta's creation of a new Class C stock announced this past week would give Zuckerberg more than $20 billion of these shares, which he could sell to pay the proposed California wealth tax without diluting his control of the company.

While passage of the billionaire tax would give a one-time boost to California's budget, Nuveen estimates a reduction of slightly less than 1% in future income taxes, Close said. That would result from the departure of the ultrawealthy to lower-tax states or countries.

In actuality, California's Proposition 3 may have more important fiscal impact than the more-publicized billionaire tax, according to Tom Kozlik, head of public policy and municipal strategy at Dallas-based HilltopSecurities. That proposal would indefinitely extend the top marginal state income-tax rates of 10.3%-12.3% to fund education. Meanwhile, the one-time proposed billionaire levy currently has long odds of getting voted in. Democratic Gov. Gavin Newsom has come out against it (possibly with an eye on a presidential run in 2028). And prediction sites Kalshi and Polymarket this past week put the probability of passage in the low-20% range.

In Florida, Kalshi and Polymarket also have the property-tax exemption proposal falling well short of the required 60% supermajority needed for it to pass. The higher homestead exemption is being sold as a property-tax reduction, though it would also have the effect of taking away funding from areas other than education, said John Mousseau, chief investment officer at Cumberland Advisors in Sarasota.

The effects of tax restrictions would hit various areas differently. For instance, Nuveen's Close observes, the Port St. Lucie area, with a higher proportion of residential real estate valued closer to the proposed exemption level, would be hit harder than Miami-Dade County, with much pricier real estate and more commercial property. Mousseau added that the tax curb would hamper funding of infrastructure needs brought on by the influx of new residents attracted by Florida's lack of an income tax.

It's understandable that Americans suffering from high prices and stagnant pay would want to seek tax relief at the ballot box. For muni investors, however, that undermines the backing of tax-supported general obligation, or GO, bonds. Mousseau added that in the rare cases of municipal bankruptcies, as seen in Puerto Rico and Detroit, the GO bondholder was treated as an unsecured creditor by the court.

One way to avoid that dilemma is for muni investors to favor revenue bonds backed by essential services and not subject to the politics of taxes. For instance, both Close and Mousseau said that investors could opt for New York City Municipal Water Finance Authority revenue bonds, with a higher credit rating, instead of New York City GOs, if they are wary of the city's Democratic Socialist mayor, Zohran Mamdani. In a similar vein, Close suggests San Francisco Public Utilities Commission Water Revenue bonds as a possible substitute for City and County of San Francisco GOs.

Former House Speaker Tip O'Neill famously observed that all politics is local. So is investing in muni bonds.

The president has repeatedly promised to bring Americans lower prices, higher growth, and more jobs. His administration has produced mixed results.

By Megan Leonhardt

Economic issues will be top of mind for voters at the polls on Nov. 3 in an election that could alter the leadership of Congress. Every seat in the U.S. House of Representatives is up for grabs, as are roughly a third of seats in the Senate. Both are currently controlled by Republicans, but Democrats are favored to win a majority in the House and possibly in the Senate.

While a president is never solely responsible for the state of the economy, this year's midterms will be a referendum, in part, on President Donald Trump's economy — the good, the bad, and the confounding.

The economy has performed well from a headline perspective in Trump's second term, with gross domestic product growth topping a solid 2% over the past six quarters. Corporate earnings have been on a tear, up by double digits in recent quarters, and the stock market has soared, minus a few stomach-churning detours. Under the hood, however, economic gains have been uneven across industries and households, and higher prices are weighing on consumer optimism.

"Inflation is the dominant story line," says Saira Malik, chief investment officer at Nuveen.

Annual inflation was up 3.7% in September from 3.4% in August. Crude oil and diesel prices, which have risen because of conflict in the Middle East, may soon feed into higher manufacturing and food costs. Trump has also raised tariffs sharply: Despite some legal defeats, the average statutory tariff rate on imports now stands at 11%, up from 2.4% in 2024.

America's mountain of debt may also be on voters' minds, particularly those of bondholders. The yield on the 10-year U.S. Treasury bond posted its largest increase in three decades in the latest quarter. It is sitting just above 5%, as buyers demand more compensation for lending to Uncle Sam. The Federal Reserve raised interest rates by a quarter of a percentage point in September, pushing the cost of servicing the government's roughly $40 trillion debt to multidecade highs.

"All of this is showing up in the polling," says Malik, whose base case is a split Congress, with the House flipping Democratic.

The seven charts below examine various economic aspects of Trump's second presidency. Expect voters to apportion both praise and blame come November.

1. Economic Growth

Growth in real gross domestic product, or GDP adjusted for inflation, has been fairly robust, averaging an annualized 2.2% in the past six quarters. That is well below 2021's stimulus-fueled postpandemic growth rate, but above the 2% rate considered healthy for an advanced economy and higher than that of nearly all other G-7 and major developed economies over the past 18 months.

Economic gains have been driven by sturdy consumer spending and strong business investment, tied largely to the buildout of artificial intelligence. U.S. leadership in AI should power even more growth over the rest of Trump's term, but the outlook for consumer spending may be less promising, suggests Shawn Snyder, an economic strategist at Potomac Fund Management.

"Higher mortgage rates, elevated gas prices for a long period of time, and the Fed tightening should slow the economy over the next six to 12 months," he says.

2. Inflation

Trump campaigned on improving affordability, but persistently elevated inflation has worsened the problem for many U.S. households. While inflation has cooled significantly from the postpandemic era, in large part because the Fed lifted interest rates, price growth recently accelerated and remains well above the central bank's 2% target.

The consumer price index has risen 5.4% since Trump took office. Grocery prices have gained 4.5%, and gasoline prices have soared 39%.

The latest bout of inflation has been exacerbated by the administration's policies, including the imposition of tariffs on many imports and launching war against Iran. Although Trump has called publicly for lower interest rates, the Fed raised its federal-funds rate target range in September to 3.75%-4%, and current Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh, a Trump nominee, has been resolute in stating that the central bank will return inflation to target.

3. Labor Market

Although monthly payroll growth has been uneven during Trump's current term, things are looking up this year. Nonfarm employers added an average of 68,000 jobs a month through September, compared with an average of just 10,000 a month in 2025.

The unemployment rate has stayed relatively stable and measured 4.2% in September, according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics' last monthly data report ahead of the midterms. The unemployment rate has ranged from 4.1% to 4.5% in the past 19 months, pointing to a tight labor market.

That is due largely to constrained labor supply. An aging workforce and stricter immigration policies have curtailed the flow of workers, leaving fewer people actively looking to fill open roles.

4. Wage Growth

Real wage and income growth have slowed during Trump's second term: Median weekly earnings haven't kept pace with inflation for the past six months.

Muted wage-growth likely reflects workers' diminished bargaining power and could persist until there is more churn in the labor market, says Robert Sockin, PGIM's chief U.S. economist. That could take a while, given fewer job openings and businesses' dulled appetite for hiring.

September's 0.1% monthly gain in hourly wage growth is problematic, as it is below the pace needed to sustain real consumer spending, writes Chris Osmond, chief investment officer at Fifth Third Wealth Advisors.

5. Stock Market

If stock market performance determined election outcomes, the president's party would clinch the vote without a fight. Stocks have soared during Trump's second term, enabling many Americans to build wealth, which encourages consumer and business spending and helps drive economic growth.

The S&P 500 gained nearly 28% from Inauguration Day through the end of September, propelled by gains in stocks tied to the boom in artificial intelligence, including the data-center buildout. The administration's deregulatory efforts and tax cuts helped to create an environment that has encouraged business investment and spending.

That said, some of Trump's policies have cost investors, at least in the short term. U.S.-traded stocks lost about 11% in the five trading days following his "Liberation Day" tariff announcement last year. And some of the market's setbacks this year were because of surging oil prices caused by the Iran war.

6. Government Debt

Federal debt has more than doubled in the past decade, to about $40.4 trillion. Roughly $4 trillion of that has accrued since the start of Trump's second term.

Debt as a percentage of economic output has declined in recent years, however, as the economy grows. The debt-to-GDP ratio peaked at 133% in the second quarter of 2020, as the government spent money to stimulate the pandemic-era economy. It has fallen to 121% as of June.

The U.S. and many other developed nations have borrowed vast sums and run large deficits in recent years, periodically rattling bond investors and sparking fears of a "debt crisis." In the U.S., both Democratic and Republican-led administrations have added to the federal debt to a similar degree, says Nuveen's Malik. An electoral sweep by either party could lead to more fiscal spending, creating more pressure on longer-term bond yields.

7. Consumer Sentiment

Consumer sentiment nosedived in 2025 and has continued to decline, notwithstanding strong GDP growth and a decent job market. This year's drop is due largely to rising gasoline prices and other affordability concerns. When prices at the pump spiked after the Iran war started, sentiment headed even lower.

The University of Michigan recorded the lowest sentiment reading on record in May and the second-lowest reading in September, both months when gas prices were particularly elevated. The monthly survey measures respondents' views on the economic outlook, including business conditions, wages, jobs, and personal finances. The university's Index of Consumer Sentiment has declined nearly 33% since Trump took office in 2025 and reflects a souring mood among Americans across the political spectrum.

Sentiment readings have fallen 20% since the start of the year among self-identified Republicans and 13% among Democrats. Respondents ages 18-54 report below-average sentiment. Older Americans are more optimistic.

Sentiment may no longer be a reliable predictor of spending momentum — the two have become increasingly divorced in recent years. But it has been a rough indicator of voting trends, in particular the prospects for the incumbent president's party.

5 Telecom Stocks That Can Survive the Musk Threat-and 1 Reason to Buy SpaceX — Barron's
data.description:
By Al Root

Telecom stocks are under siege, and the enemy is SpaceX. Investors fear that the emergence of a well-capitalized SpaceX and its huge, fully reusable Starship will take over telecommunications, artificial intelligence, and maybe everything else. Elon Musk doesn't disagree: He recently said his SpaceX could be worth more than Earth.

Take a deep breath, folks. SpaceX will eventually launch a mobile telecom business, but not as soon as investors fear and not in the way investors imagine. There are still plenty of stocks in the sector that could pay off.

You wouldn't know it by the prices. Shares of Verizon Communications, AT&T, and T-Mobile US fell an average of 11% on Oct. 9, the day after SpaceX announced its purchase of low-band spectrum from Grain Management. The spectrum, which is good at penetrating obstacles such as buildings, brought SpaceX a step closer to offering mobile service, directly competing with the traditional industry.

Disruption fears have been a sector overhang for months, leaving the three stocks off an average of about 25% from their 52-week highs.

SpaceX is clearly a threat, but it will take Musk's rocket and AI company years and billions of dollars to fully develop its offering, according to Citi analyst Michael Rollins. SpaceX will need terrestrial infrastructure and maybe even a traditional wireless partner.

The most at risk appear to be cable companies that face competition on all fronts, from broadband to the home to mobile telecom. Wireless operators, by contrast, have the scale, experience, and spectrum to survive.

Here are six communications stocks that investors should look to when evaluating the future of wireless telecom. They just might defy the doomsayers.

TMUS

T-Mobile US already has a space-to-cell partnership with SpaceX. It has a lot more wireless spectrum, the pipes that carry wireless data, than SpaceX has amassed — about 400 megahertz to SpaceX's 80. Earnings are expected to grow by about 24% annually for the coming two years, about 11 percentage points better than AT&T and 18 percentage points better than Verizon.

The shares are priced nicely, too. They trade at about 12.5 times expected earnings over the coming 12 months, the lowest valuation ratio in more than a decade. Things can always get worse, but shares look attractive at these levels.

T

AT&T reported better-than-expected third-quarter numbers on Wednesday. Still, shares fell 6.4%, reflecting the dour sentiment. But AT&T's results "bode well" for 2027 numbers, says Rollins. He recommended buying the dip after AT&T shares fell following SpaceX's low-band spectrum purchase. Rollins kept his Buy rating on shares after third-quarter earnings. His price target is $28, up nearly 25% from current levels. J.P. Morgan analyst Sebastiano Petti calls AT&T a "top pick" and has a price target of $31.

CCI

Crown Castle provides wireless telecom infrastructure.

It's a real estate investment trust that owns more than 40,000 cell towers. Crown and peers American Tower REIT and SBA Communications are the apartment buildings of the wireless communications world, renting rooms to Verizon and the like. SpaceX represents a new tenant, and more tenants mean more rent for Crown Castle. Bernstein analyst Madison Rezaei rates shares Outperform and has a $92 price target. As a REIT, it is sensitive to interest rates and has income — a yield of 5.4%, to be exact.

VSAT

Viasat operates a network of roughly two dozen high-capacity satellites providing communications services to, among others, airlines and maritime businesses. It's seeing competition from Starlink, but is growing its business with military customers — looking to wean off, well, Starlink. It also has a valuable portfolio of wireless spectrum.

William Blair analyst Louie DiPalma figures Viasat is worth about $20 billion, well above its enterprise value of about $14 billion. He rates the shares Outperform.

ASTS

AST SpaceMobile is a critical partner for the traditional telecom industry as it wages war with SpaceX.

Sure, shares have been hammered in recent months, down almost 70% from a 52-week high north of $130 — and down almost 30% since SpaceX announced its low-band spectrum purchase. But that drop was "misguided," says Deutsche Bank analyst Bryan Kraft. For starters, the SpaceX spectrum purchase doesn't put SpaceX in direct competition with AST. It aims to provide coverage in dead zones for the traditional industry. Kraft rates shares a Buy. Target share price: $93.

SPCX

SpaceX, yes, SpaceX — and its 64 times price/earnings ratio — is a good bet. Sure, most of the company's valuation is built on AI dreams. But the Starlink business ended the third quarter with 13.6 million subscribers and generated earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization, or Ebitda, of $3.5 billion, up 35% year over year. Morgan Stanley analyst Adam Jonas says SpaceX's communications business is worth $115 a share. That's about 70% of the current stock price, meaning that investors get the space and AI businesses at a discount. Jonas' target for the entire business: $300.

data.description: US stocks fell on Friday as selling pressure spread from AI-related trades to broader market sectors. The Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 652.82 points, or 1.23%, to 52,215.16, with a weekly gain of 0.41%. The S&P 500 dropped 39.75 points, or 0.52%, to 7,623.68, down 0.47% for the week. The Nasdaq Composite fell 53.51 points, or 0.21%, to 25,955.34, posting a weekly decline of 0.71%, according to Sina Finance. Most major technology stocks declined, with Google falling over 1%, and Amazon and Meta each dropping nearly 1%. SpaceX rose over 1%, while storage sector shares advanced, with SK Hynix up over 4% and Micron Technology gaining over 2%. Oil and gas stocks surged, with Chevron, ExxonMobil, and Shell each rising over 2%. Defensive sectors came under pressure, with consumer staples, utilities, and healthcare all declining. Dow component American Express fell over 3% after announcing plans to cut approximately 5% of its global workforce, citing the need to prepare for AI. Caterpillar dropped about 2%, and Goldman Sachs declined over 1%, further weighing on the Dow. Over the past two weeks, investors have been pulling out of tech stocks and data center beneficiaries, shifting toward safe assets, said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management. Ellerbroek added that tech company earnings this quarter have proven strong, giving investors reason to embrace tech stocks and reduce sentiment-driven de-risking. The 10-year Treasury yield stood at approximately 4.999%, rising over 4 basis points on the day. Oil prices rose further, pressuring equities. December WTI crude futures gained 3.80 to settle at 103.27 per barrel, up 3.82%, while December Brent crude climbed 3.55 to 116.72 per barrel, up 3.14%. Reports indicated that the United States and Israel may be developing plans for another strike on Iran, as part of a regional conflict that began in late February. Iran stated it was also prepared to retaliate.

data.title: Lunit and Summit Therapeutics Announce Agreement to Apply AI-powered SCOPE IO Platform for Tumor Microenvironment Analysis in Immuno-Oncology Development
data.description:
Research Will Use Lunit's AI-powered Pathology Platform to Analyze H&E Whole-Slide Images and Generate Scalable Insights into Tumor Microenvironment Biology

SEOUL, South Korea, Oct. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Lunit Inc. () and Summit Therapeutics Inc. () today announced a research agreement to evaluate the use of Lunit SCOPE IO, Lunit's AI-powered pathology platform, for tumor microenvironment analysis in support of Summit's immuno-oncology development programs with ivonescimab.

The effort will focus on applying Lunit SCOPE IO to hematoxylin and eosin-stained (H&E) whole-slide images to characterize tumor microenvironment features. The companies aim to explore how AI-powered pathology analysis can support biomarker discovery, patient stratification or selection, and a deeper biological understanding of response to ivonescimab therapies.

Summit is developing ivonescimab, a novel, potential first-in-class investigational PD-1 / VEGF bispecific antibody, in several solid tumors. Lunit SCOPE IO is designed to support immuno-oncology research and biomarker development through AI-powered analysis of H&E slides, enabling scalable assessment of tumor microenvironment features without requiring additional stains or assays.

"Understanding the tumor microenvironment is increasingly important as immuno-oncology moves beyond single-axis checkpoint inhibition toward more complex mechanisms and combinations," said Allen Yang, MD, PhD, Chief Research and Development Strategy Officer of Summit. "We are pleased to work with Lunit to explore how AI-powered pathology can help generate deeper, more scalable insights from routine tissue samples and inform the continued development of ivonescimab."

"Summit is at the forefront of next-generation immuno-oncology development, and we are excited to support its efforts with Lunit SCOPE IO," said Brandon Suh, Lunit CEO. "By extracting quantitative, spatially resolved immune and tumor microenvironment features from standard H&E slides, we believe SCOPE IO can help biopharma partners better understand which patients may benefit from immuno-oncology therapies and why."

This agreement reflects the growing importance of computational pathology in oncology drug development. Routine H&E slides contain rich information about tumor architecture, immune infiltration, stromal organization, and spatial interactions within the tumor microenvironment. However, traditional manual assessment can be difficult to scale and may not fully capture the quantitative and spatial complexity of the tumor-immune interface. AI-powered analysis offers the potential to convert these routinely generated pathology images into reproducible, high-dimensional biomarker data.

The companies expect the work to generate tumor microenvironment insights that may inform future translational research, exploratory biomarker strategies, and clinical development planning. No clinical outcome data are being announced as part of this release.

*Lunit SCOPE products are for research use only. Not for use in diagnostic procedures or decisions.

About Ivonescimab

Ivonescimab, known as SMT112 in Summit's license territories, North America, South America, Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Japan, and as AK112 outside of Summit's license territories, is a novel, potential first-in-class investigational bispecific antibody combining the effects of immunotherapy via a blockade of PD-1 with the anti-angiogenesis effects associated with blocking VEGF into a single molecule. By design, ivonescimab displays unique cooperative binding to each of its intended targets with multifold higher affinity to PD-1 when in the presence of VEGF.

This design is intended to differentiate ivonescimab as there is potentially higher expression (presence) of both PD-1 and VEGF in tumor tissue and the tumor microenvironment (TME) as compared to normal tissue in the body. Summit believes ivonescimab's specifically engineered tetravalent structure (four binding sites) enables higher avidity (accumulated strength of multiple binding interactions) in the TME (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025). This tetravalent structure, the intentional novel design of the molecule, and bringing these two targets into a single bispecific antibody with cooperative binding qualities have the potential to direct ivonescimab to the tumor tissue versus healthy tissue. The intent of ivonescimab's design, together with a half-life of 6 to 7 days after the first dose (Zhong, et al, iScience, 2025) increasing to approximately 10 days at steady state dosing, is to improve upon previously established efficacy thresholds, side effects, and safety profiles associated with prior approved drugs to these targets.

Ivonescimab was invented by Akeso Inc. (HKEX Code: 9926.HK) and is currently utilized in multiple Phase III clinical trials. Over 5,000 patients have been treated with ivonescimab in clinical studies globally and over 100,000 patients when considering those treated in a commercial setting in China, as noted by Akeso.

There are currently 17 Phase III clinical studies that are either announced, ongoing, or have been completed studying ivonescimab, five of which are Summit-sponsored global studies, two of which are studies sponsored by cooperative groups, and 10 of which are being or have been conducted in China by Akeso. Summit began its clinical development of ivonescimab in NSCLC (HARMONi, HARMONi-3, HARMONi-7) and expanded its sponsored Phase III clinical development program into colorectal cancer (CRC; HARMONi-GI3) and urothelial carcinoma (bladder cancer; HARMONi-GU1). The two cooperative studies are in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC; ILLUMINE) and biliary tract cancer (BTC; EA2251).

Five Phase III ivonescimab clinical trials have read out to date, all five with positive data. Four of these five studies are in NSCLC and one is in BTC. In addition to Summit's positive HARMONi study in NSCLC, Akeso has had positive read-outs in four single-region (China), randomized Phase III clinical trials, HARMONi-A, HARMONi-2, HARMONi-6 (each in NSCLC), and HARMONi-GI1 (in BTC) for ivonescimab, including a statistically significant overall survival benefit in all four studies from China.

Akeso is actively conducting additional Phase III clinical studies in settings outside of NSCLC and biliary-tract cancer, including triple-negative breast cancer, head and neck squamous cell carcinoma, small cell lung cancer, colorectal cancer, and pancreatic cancer.

Ivonescimab is an investigational therapy that is not approved by any regulatory authority in Summit's license territories, including the United States and Europe. Ivonescimab was initially approved for marketing authorization in China in May 2024.

Our clinically validated solutions span medical imaging, breast health, and biomarker analysis, empowering earlier detection, smarter treatment decisions, and more precise outcomes across the cancer care continuum.

data.title: Typhoon Champi sweeps past Taiwan, one dead and 500 injured
data.description:
Typhoon Champi swept past Taiwan on Saturday killing one person and injuring more than 500, downing trees and severing power, as it continues to weaken and head north towards the Chinese coast.

At one point a super typhoon and one of the strongest storms in the Pacific this year, Champi is weakening though still packing gusts of around 126 kph (78 mph) near its centre, according to Taiwan's Central Weather Administration (CWA).

The storm was about 150 km (93 miles) east of Taiwan, the CWA said, having glanced the island's northeast coast in the early hours of Saturday.

The storm's forecast track shows it is now turning north toward the Chinese coast and eventually move into southern Japan.

Taiwan's fire department said the death toll remaining at one, a man swept away by waves from the island of Liuqiu, with 527 injuries during the heavy wind and torrential rain.

Taipower said at one point more than 167,000 homes had lost electricity, though most had been reconnected.

The transport ministry said 242 flights were cancelled, though that was an improvement from Friday when the number was almost 1,000.

In the capital Taipei, there were downed trees and on-off squally rain showers.

A swathe of northern and central Taiwan, including Taipei, declared a second day of office and school closures on Saturday.

Taiwan is generally very well prepared for typhoons, which keeps casualties low. Although more common in summer, the storms can strike in autumn too.
